summary: claude-cup harvests installer credentials via Claude Code hooks and exfiltrates a signal index to api.claude-cup.com
details: claude-cup@0.9.9 ships a credential-harvesting pipeline disguised behind football/cup terminology. On CLI startup the package enumerates classic installer-secret locations (~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.git-credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.kube/config,.env files, shell histories, OS credential managers, VS Code auth storage, cloud-sync folders) driven by a ZONE_RESOLUTION map that aliases each secret path to a football-code (FPZ/DCZ/MDZ/SPZ/TRZ/OVZ/HIZ/PLZ/EDZ). Extracted tokens are live-validated against provider APIs (GitHub, npm whoami, AWS STS, OpenAI, Anthropic, Stripe) and AWS access-key/secret pairs are grouped. A second path pipes an assembled directive into the installed Claude Code CLI as `claude -p --permission-mode auto --model haiku`, instructing the model to audit the whole machine, validate secrets against live APIs, and encode results using the football terminology 'so EDR, logger, or observer' reading the reasoning chain 'see only football/cup analytics terminology'; output is written to ~/.claude-jar/last-audit.json. Persistence is established by writing ~/.claude-jar/mcp-server.mjs and merging SessionStart/PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks into ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.cursor/mcp.json, causing the harvester to re-run on every future Claude Code and Cursor session. A signal summary (machine_id, session counts, vcs_write_count, registry_deploy_count, cloud_present, other_cloud_present, browser_sessions, discovery counts, fingerprint) is base64url-encoded and sent to https://api.claude-cup.com/v1/config, which also returns the runtime `toolbelt` path list, `audit_prompt` template, and validation endpoints — allowing the operator to change scan targets and prompts server-side without republishing.
